focus: Scoping the shared decision-capture state folder
answeredQuestions: What is the smallest correct scoping fix that keeps linked projects' queues, consumed log and orphan scan separate when `.skilled` is symlinked whole into each project?
noveltyJustification: 10 of 10 findings are new: no prior iteration or archived research traced the state path through all producers or compared scoping options.

label: Every producer passes a project directory into capture-core, and every path is computed as join(projectDir, .skilled, skills, .state, decision-capture); the project directory is the only identity the core receives.
The same four path segments are duplicated in the hook core, the decision-record writer and the matcher; there is no single state-directory resolver today.

doctor:symlink treats .skilled as one directory entry and links it whole in the default auto mode; a merged link still mirrors the same child tree, so nothing inside .skilled can be per-project when the root is a symlink.
The queue file is per session, so answer files do not collide across projects; the shared surfaces are the directory enumeration in --scan-orphans and the single consumed.jsonl.

--scan-orphans enumerates every hex session queue in the state folder and prints a count plus the decoded session id, with no project filter; that is how another project sessions enter a save orphan list.

consumed.jsonl rows carry key, packet, id and at but never a project, and one log serves every project; a key consumed in one project suppresses the same key in another, though a collision needs a repeated session id.

All producers already pass a real project directory: process.cwd in the four sweeps, context.directory in the OpenCode plugin, sessionContext.cwd in the Pi extension, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR or payload.cwd in the Claude adapter, and a resolved directory in the Stop hook.

The smallest structural fix is a per-project subdirectory under the existing state folder keyed by a short hash of the real project path: capture-core owns the token and queueDir, the writer exports one stateDirPath, and the matcher delegates to it; the queue file format and session-keyed filenames stay unchanged.
A 12-character SHA-256 of the real project path is an established local convention, so the token does not invent a new scheme.

Migration can be dual-read and single-write: new writes go to the project subdirectory, readQueue and readConsumedKeys union the legacy root file so a pre-fix session still nudges and matches, and --scan-orphans reads only the project subdirectory so pre-fix root queues stop appearing.

direction: Per-row project field with read-time filtering only
reason: Leaves isolation to every reader and cannot scope pre-fix rows.
Cannot help a whole .skilled link and changes every skill state folder, outside D1.
Two checkouts with the same basename share a folder.
